title: Wing Tank Access Panel Closure Standard with a Retained Face Seal and a Single Torque Sequence
abstract: Proposal to replace the wet-sealed wing tank access panel closure by a retained face seal with a single published torque sequence, so that a tank entry no longer produces a weeping panel a month later.

sections.reason: Roughly one tank entry in three produces a weeping panel within a month of closure, and the weep almost always appears at the same two positions on the panel. Across a fleet performing ninety tank entries a year that is thirty repeat defects, each consuming a night stop, and two first-sector cancellations in the last twelve months when an overnight weep became a drip. The closure today depends on a wet sealant bead applied by hand and on a torque sequence that exists in three different published forms, which is why the result varies with the individual mechanic. A second operator and one large maintenance organisation report the same rate independently.
sections.description: The wet-sealed closure is replaced by a machined groove in the panel face carrying a retained elastomeric seal, with the sealant reduced to a fillet at the panel edge for aerodynamic smoothness only. The transmitter D2810138674936 mounted through the panel is replaced by an item with a matching face seal boss, and the clamp ROD517260-78 that carries the internal harness across the panel is relocated so that it no longer bears on the seal groove. The protective sleeve AGS540148-51 is fitted at each fastener to stop the seal being nipped during closure, and the switch BE49012-14 is renewed because its flange thickness changes with the new groove. The valve at FIN 44QT is disturbed for access and refitted. A single torque sequence replaces the three published variants. Work is in zones 593, 692 and 595 with the tank drained, purged and ventilated. The panel arrangement is on drawing D28101115502.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 4.8 kilograms per aircraft across the eight modified panels, symmetric about the centre line. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable: the groove is machined into the panel at embodiment and an unmodified panel has no seat for the retained seal. The panel closure task loses the sealant cure hold, which shortens a tank entry by four hours, and the repeat weep inspection is deleted. The fuel tank access task, the parts figure, the sealing and bonding standard practice reference and the tank entry safety instructions all require re-issue.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, embodied one wing at a time during any visit at which the tank is already open. The machining of the groove is the pacing operation and is proposed as a bench task on removed panels rather than in situ. No production cut-in is proposed because the current line standard already uses a different panel.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether the panels can be machined off the aircraft within a normal tank entry window or whether an exchange pool is needed, whether the retained seal is compatible with the fuel additive package used by two of the requesting operators, whether the interfay sealing standard released for fuselage joints applies to this closure, and what the reduced sealant bead does to the published lightning protection assessment for the tank boundary.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric about the centre line, no measurable effect
type_data.production_impact: No cut-in; the current line standard uses a different panel
